To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the two reference models under analysis are both suitable to be used in the design of e-commerce applications, but the one based on UML and the one based on the e-commerce reference architecture are more suitable for the design of e-business applications and e-business applications with business processes, respectively.
the reference models are similar in terms of the number of components and their relationships.

(i) the reference models analyzed are similar in terms of their overall structure and in the way the concepts are organized; (ii) they differ in terms of the concepts that are included and excluded, and in the way they are defined; and (iii) the two reference models are similar in the level of abstraction at which the concepts are defined.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an evaluation framework that can be used to compare and select reference models, and that can be adapted to the needs of the particular system under design.
the development of an approach for the comparative analysis and selection of reference models.

the development and evaluation of a conceptual framework for the comparison of reference models, and the application of that framework to the comparative analysis and evaluation of two reference models for electronic business.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ECR model is better suited for a B2C environment, while the E-Commerce Reference Model is better suited for B2B.

, while the two reference models are similar with regard to their overall architecture, they differ in terms of their underlying assumptions and in the level of support they provide for the different aspects of an electronic commerce application.
, in the case of electronic commerce, the reference model of the University of Hamburg (UoH) has the potential to better serve the needs of the system developers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reference model selection is not a trivial task.
we have developed a framework for the comparative analysis of reference models, which is based on the elaboration of a linguistic classification scheme.

, in general, we can conclude that, for the two reference models analyzed, the quality of the reference model is determined by the quality of the underlying reference architecture, and the quality of the associated reference processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the quality of reference models should not be evaluated only in terms of their completeness and correctness, but rather in terms of the extent to which they are able to capture the complexity and the dynamics of the domain to be modelled.
the proposed approach provides a structured way of evaluating reference models.
the quality of a reference model depends on the quality of the model’s underlying language.
